pages.title: Postcards and travel messages

situation.text: You are on vacation at the beach. You write a short postcard and a travel message to your family and friends: where you are, how it is and when you will see them.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can write a short postcard and a travel message: greet, say how you are, describe the place and say goodbye.
canDo: Say how it is: Having a great time! The beach is beautiful.
Use the postcard phrase: Wish you were here!
Close and sign: See you soon! Love, …
success: I say where I am and how it is.
I use Wish you were here or See you soon.
pages.think: When you travel, do you send messages to your family? Short or long? Photos or text?

teach.goal: Abrir pela situação real: escrever um cartão-postal ou mensagem de viagem. Aula com forte foco em escrita curta.
solo: Pergunte como o aluno costuma avisar a família quando viaja.
group: Cada aluno diz uma coisa que escreveria em um cartão.
extra: Do you like to receive postcards?
Do you keep photos from trips?
support: Aceite respostas curtas e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Ask real questions about travel messages; keep it light.
intro.group: One question per student, then a question to a classmate.

pages.recall: Last class: tourist information. Ask: What can we see in your city? Is it open today?

qs.q: Do you send messages when you travel?

pages.tip: Use the answers to recycle places and weather words.

teach.goal: Entrar no tema e retomar informações turísticas.
extra: What is the weather like today?

errors.w: I send message for my mother.
errors.r: I send a message to my mother.

errors.w: I like very much the beach.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — postcard conventions
pages.intro: A postcard is short: a small space, a few lines. Look at the cards and guess how English-speaking travelers write.

cards.note: A classic postcard phrase: you miss the person and share the view.
On a postcard, the address goes on the right side and the message on the left; the stamp goes in the top right corner.
Postcards usually say the good things: the weather, the food, the views.

qs.q: What do people usually write on a postcard?
qs.pt: O que as pessoas costumam escrever em um cartão-postal?

levels.A2: Where I am, the weather and how I am.
levels.B1: A short greeting, where you are, what you do, and a goodbye.
levels.B2: A quick snapshot of the trip with a positive tone, ending with a warm goodbye.

qs.q: What does “Wish you were here!” mean?
qs.pt: O que significa “Wish you were here!”?

levels.A2: I want you to be here with me.
levels.B1: I wish you could enjoy this place with me.
levels.B2: A friendly phrase that shares the moment and shows affection.

qs.q: How do you end a message to a friend?
qs.pt: Como você termina uma mensagem para um amigo?

levels.B1: See you soon! Take care. Love, Kai.
levels.B2: Use See you soon! with Love, Hugs or Best wishes, depending on how close you are.

pages.compare: In Brazil, people also write “Saudades!” and “Beijos” on postcards. In English, “Wish you were here!” and “Love,” are similar. What do you write?

teach.goal: Mostrar convenções de cartão-postal: curto, positivo, “Wish you were here!”, endereço à direita, selo no canto superior direito, despedida e assinatura. Verdadeiro para cartões em inglês dos EUA e Reino Unido.
solo: Mostre os cartões e peça hipóteses.
group: Cada aluno escolhe um cartão e explica.
answers: Q1: onde está, tempo, como está.
Q2: queria que você estivesse aqui.
Q3: See you soon! + Love, + nome.
extra: Do you write cards on paper?
Do you prefer postcards or messages?
stretch: B2: qual a diferença de tom entre “Love,” e “Best wishes,”?

pass1.pt: O que o Kai está fazendo?

teach.goal: Entender a situação e 4 informações: destinatária, tempo, selo e caixa de correio.

qs.q: How does Kai end the postcard?
Where does Kai put the postcard?

retell.prompt: Retell what Kai writes on the postcard.

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, notar os chunks do cartão e recontar.
solo: O aluno lê o Kai; você lê a Una.
answers: grandma · sunny and hot · See you soon! Love, Kai · mailbox
support: Mostre o PT após a 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.use: Say you are enjoying the trip.
Say goodbye and promise to meet.
Sign a message to family or close friends.

pages.note: Choose 4 expressions (★) to use again and again. “Having a great time” drops “I am”: it is common in short messages.

teach.goal: Escolher 4 chunks para o cartão e a função de cada um.
solo: Peça um exemplo para alguém real.
group: Cada aluno escolhe um chunk e explica.
answers: Opening · Feeling · Missing someone · Goodbye · Signing
extra: Which one is for a close friend?

errors.w: I am having a great time (em cartão curto, muito formal).

patterns.name: Short feeling phrases
patterns.formula: **Having** + a great time / fun / a wonderful trip

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: We are having a wonderful time.
I wish you could be here with us.
I look forward to seeing you soon.
register.note: Postcards and quick messages use short forms; formal letters use full sentences.

teach.goal: Fixar 2 padrões principais: Having a great time e The… is…. Em cartão se omite “I am”.
solo: Use a troca de palavras com a viagem do aluno.
group: Em pares: um escolhe as peças, o outro fala.
teach.answers: Padrões 01 e 02 são o foco; 03 é expansão.
extra: Describe your last trip in two short sentences.

errors.w: We are having a good time and the food are great.

support: Fique só com Having a great time!
stretch: Escrever um cartão de 4 frases sem apoio.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — linking sounds
pages.tip: In “Wish you were here” the sounds join: “wish-you” sounds like “wi-shoo”. In “See you soon” the sounds join too: “see-you”. Say it in one flow.

own.prompt: Write your own closing for a postcard (e.g. See you …) and say it in one flow.
own.criteria: Say it twice. Do the words join, without pauses?

teach.goal: UM fenômeno: ligação entre palavras (wish-you, see-you).
group: Cada aluno diz a própria despedida.
answers: Identify 1: Wish you were here! · Identify 2: See you soon!

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. You start a postcard to your friend Ana.
2. You say you are enjoying the trip.

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado com abertura, descrição e despedida.
solo: Se acertar rápido, peça a versão para um amigo próximo.
answers: 1: Dear Ana, · 2: Having a great time! · 3: Wish you were here! · 4: See you soon! Love, Kai
Gap: Having · were · The beach is beautiful. · See you on Friday! · Great! Having a wonderful time.
extra: Write the first line of your own postcard.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — travel messages

brief.teacher: You are a friend on the phone. Ask about the trip and what to write on the postcard.
brief.student: You are on vacation: say how it is, describe the place and plan to see your friend.

orders: A beach vacation with the family
A city trip to see museums
complications: Your friend asks “What’s the weather like?” — answer.
Your friend asks for a photo: describe it.
You forgot a word: describe it with other words.
Ask your friend what to write on a card.
success: I say how the trip is.

solo: Use a viagem real ou sonhada do aluno.
Rodada 1 com chunks; 2 palavras-chave; 3 sem roteiro.

stretch: Contar o que fizeram hoje usando 2 verbos no passado.

group: Troque os pares a cada rodada.
Cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.
No gap: A sabe para quem e onde; B sabe o tempo e a despedida.
answers: A: Dear Mom; the beach. B: sunny and hot; See you soon!

pages.goal: Each group writes and reads aloud a short postcard from a different trip.

teach.goal: Escrever e ler em voz alta um cartão curto.
group: Cada grupo escreve em conjunto e escolhe quem lê.
Rodada 1 com apoio, 2 palavras-chave, 3 sem roteiro.
answers: Modelo: “Dear Grandma, Having a great time! The beach is beautiful. Wish you were here! Love, Kai”

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a postcard or a travel message to a family member or friend. Say where you are, how it is, and say goodbye.
pages.model: Dear Grandma, Having a great time at the beach! It’s sunny and hot, and the food is delicious. Wish you were here! See you soon! Love, Kai
checklist: I opened with Dear… or Hi…
I said where I am and how it is.
I used Wish you were here or See you soon.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita central da aula: cartão-postal curto.
support: Dê o modelo e peça que troquem os dados.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: The structure stays the same; language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: Having a great time! Wish you were here!
We’re at the beach. It’s sunny and the food is great. See you soon!
We’ve been swimming every day and I’ve already taken about a hundred photos!
Although the weather wasn’t perfect at first, the trip has turned out to be exactly what we needed.
It’s the kind of place that makes you forget your inbox exists, and I wouldn’t mind staying another week.
Words fail me, so I’ll let the view do the talking; you’d love it here.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o aluno está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do seu nível e a do próximo.
